Today, June 23rd, 2026, we took our cat Smokey to be examined for a rash on his forehead.  We asked to see our regular vet, Dr. Birchler,  who we hold in good standing.  Instead we were seen By Dr. Valdes for reasons we do not know.  Dr. Valdes told us our cat would need to be sedated, so he could do a full examination.  We asked him how long it would take, and he replied one hour.  He also said we could wait in the reception area.  We decided to go to lunch in the area while the examination took place.  We returned two hours later and asked for Smokey's status.  We were told Dr. Valdes was under the impression we were going home and nothing had been done yet.  We never said we were going home.  We were livid.  TWO HOURS AND ABSOLUTELY NOTHING WAS DONE. This is not just annoying for us, this is traumatizing for the cat sitting in a strange place and probably forgotten about.  Even if we went home, two hours of absolutely nothing being done when we were told the exam would take an hour is unacceptable.  This was very inconsiderate.  We demanded a refund of our deposit back and the immediate return of our cat.  We were our refund would take 3-5 days.  I find that odd since it was paid via debit and they were quick to take the very expensive deposit.  Furthermore, Dr. Valdes would not even come out and talk to us our apologize.  This is inconsiderate and indifferent behavior on Dr. Valdes part.  This was absolutely our worst experience dealing with a vet.  We never want to see this doctor again, and are considering using a different animal hospital in the future.

Great with pets!! Always busy and crowded so its best to have an appointment. Doctors and staff are amazing, patient, kind, and welcoming. They handle your pets with care and definitely help them. Me and my feline 🐈 loves it here.

A special thank you to Dr. Mittal, who was incredibly compassionate, kindhearted, and caring throughout Kikis final battle with cancer. During such a difficult time, Dr. Mittal and the entire staff treated both our cat and our family with genuine empathy and respect.

very professional kind and knowledgable service. I walked in when they opened and my pet was able to be seen within an hour.

My family and I have been taking our fur babies here for almost ten years but I’ll speak on my personal experience. My boxer Caleb had environmental allergies in which I had to take him here every 4-6weeks for routine cytopoint shots. He got to know the techs on a regular basis and we developed a really great relationship with them there. During his last year of life his health declined out of no where and Dr. Mistry (who I specifically requested almost his entire adult life) was able to feel a mass and thanks to her suggestion for imaging and recommendation for special surgery we were able to identify he had a mass on his spleen that had to be removed. Turned out to be an adrenal tumor which is a risky mass to remove.

Unfortunately the morning of his surgery at a different animal hospital for special surgery his mass erupted. They rushed him into surgery, I begged to do anything and everything to save him no matter the cost and blood transfusions and at the end of it, he didn’t make it. To say the least it was the worst day of my life and took years to recover from-I still get emotional with flashbacks.

Later on in the week after my boxer passed, i received a sympathy card in the mail from Dr. Mistry and was signed by staff in the office including the techs. I couldn’t believe they were probably in contact with Caleb’s surgeon / hospital probably following up on updates only to find out the news.

Dr. Mistry I can’t ever thank you enough for your compassion, attention to detail, patience and the love you had for our dog and I’m sure all of your patients. You are a true light in a lot of people’s lives and it is clear you love what you do. The card and thought still sticks with me til this day. One day I hope to stop by if you are still there to say hello and give you hug.

Thank you Lefferts for everything you do!

They used to be much better. Now the service quality is poor. I had been going there for years until recently. I have two cats, and one of them since kittenhood, I was told by a different vet clinic in my old neighborhood, that he likely had food allergies since he would vomit after eating any food with chicken. After I moved, I commented the same to them and they took it somewhat lightly but advised me on limited ingredient diets (we had been on royal PR but the vet here didn’t want to extend the prescription). In any case, fast forward 7 years, my same cat is experiencing terrible diarrhea, vomiting and inappetence. I rushed him in, and all I was told was that he’d been given anti diarrheal and fluids. I wasn’t given many answers as to what the hell was happening. We did x-ray and the cat hadn’t swallowed anything but that was about it. I commented on the inappetence and the doctor said since it had only been a few days he’d still be ok. My cat used to weight 19lbs in sept ‘23 when I took him for a regular check up. By April ‘24 he was quickly dropping weight. He was at 16lbs bc he wasn’t eating much of anything without vomiting. My instinct told me to take him elsewhere because I was not gonna receive any answers here, but they def charged me $500 for the x-ray and fluids. My cat had had blood work prior, in sept, and in April when I took him. Bloodwork showed amylase higher than normal. That however never triggered any curiosity here. I ended up taking my pet to Bondvet at forest hills for a second opinion, and that very likely saved his life. We struggled a lot. My cat lost 8 lbs in 2 months but I can tell you that he was thoroughly examined, every test that was called for was ordered and done. Just as I had mentioned before, which was in the cat’s medical records, my cat likely suffers from a poultry allergy which triggers what appears to be IBD. I strongly believed that had I stayed at lefferts AH, my Rio would no longer be with me today.
In the end, it is a bit more affordable than bond vet, but I would’ve ended up paying $500 for a x ray at bond vet if I had gone earlier and they would’ve actually been able to give me answers and treatment options. Bond vet is the hero in this story, and Dr Diaz saved my cat with her patience, professionalism, caring and true diagnostic seeking steps. Lefferts now seems like a negligent money grabbing scheme.
My Rio is now back on track to being a happy elder. He’s been on corticosteroids for a bit and it was quite a turn around for him. I now know that beef, which is what he was eating when the episode began, cause him allergic inflammation and trigger IBD. Just take care if you go the lefferts. They might not either know to properly diagnose or they might not care. I’m glad I sought a second opinion.

I had a horrible experience yesterday when dealing with the staff and  two “veterinarian’s” regarding my dog. Both Dr. Matt and Dr. Dr. Zachary Zalewski lack of empathy and compassion left me in tears while trying to find care for my dog.

My dog is a patient at this office, he was seen Tuesday and had some work up done. That visit went well. Upon leaving I was told to bring back a stool sample and bring my dog back if he had vomiting or diarrhea. My dog had been experiencing both since Wednesday. This was exclaimed multiple times when I contacted the office yesterday. Unfortunately, I tried to care for my dog at home, with a bland diet hoping everything would subside but as he seemed better on Thursday by Saturday he was again exhibiting abnormal symptoms and behaviors.

Yesterday, I called this office. To start the automated recording clearly states “Walk-ins” are accepted so I did not assume I would be turned away, with urgent concerns and be told the schedule is booked. When speaking to Dr. Matt, he turned my situation into a money grab. Stating, “The schedule is booked, I am unable to see you. Then following up with I can help you, and have you seen, but I am marking this appointment as an emergency visit and charging you $160.” I questioned why, as I was told from my previous visit that I should bring him back is these symptoms became present. He responded, “I can make the decision to reason for the appointment how I want, and I am marking this as an emergency visit, or, you can’t wait to have him seen on Monday, or, take him to the ER and pay more.”

In the interim, I had an incoming call from the office. Hoping that I would be assisted by some else, I hung up and picked up the incoming call. It was Dr. Zalewski. After explaining everything and at this point I was crying because I could see he wasn’t showing empathy, he responded and told me “I’m sure no one at our office told you, you could bring him back because that’s not how we operate” I was taken aback cause now I was being basically called a liar. When I asked him, so now you’re telling me I’m lying, he hung up in my face.

Not one time was my dog’s health prioritized. Not one time was my emotion acknowledged or consoled. I’m am disappointed and disgusted. No integrity was shown and I will NEVER bring my dog back,

I know you get charged for Service I was prepared to pay A estimate of $40-$60 but $140 that’s outrageous For just Give me pointers on how to keep it warm that’s why it loses 2 stars.

I came on here thinking it was the new clinic Dr. Halpern was in & mistakenly clicked the old clinic .
I realized a few reviews that caught my eye & kind of pissed me off & I truly wish Dr. Halpern was still at Lefferts. I have followed him everywhere he has moved because I trust him 1000% with my animals. I cannot speak about other doctors here because I’ve had different experiences with most of them and I’m not here to leave a bad review. I am only leaving 5 starts for HIM.

For over 15 years, not once have I doubted Dr. Halpern’s care, judgment, or integrity. He has treated and helped over 40 of my own pets, as well as animals belonging to my family and friends. Every single time, he has been professional, compassionate, honest, and direct.
He does not rush to diagnose just to give an answer, he takes the time to figure out the actual problem, and he usually does so quickly and accurately. Even in emergencies, he is the first person I call. He has never guided me in the wrong direction and always works with me to find the best options for my pet and my financial situation.

Before believing negative accusations online, I encourage people to look at long-term client experiences here AND in other locations he has been . I would trust Dr. Halpern with any animal I bring in — without hesitation.
If he ever moved far away, I would literally travel to continue having him care for my pets. That’s how much confidence I have in him. I highly recommend looking into Dr. Halpern’s education, professional history, and LEVEL of experience before believing claims that simply don’t align with the care he consistently provides.

By far the best veterinarian I have ever encountered, and I will always appreciate the dedication and heart he brings to his work.

If these doctors are supposed to keep up with your pets charts, and tell you what’s wrong with them, why would they give a pet who is very sensitive to anesthesia and sedatives another sedative injection knowing her health condition and age. If I could give 0 stars I would. We were loyal clients at this practice for 5–6 years, but after what happened to our dog Ebony, we will never return and will not be bringing our remaining pets here.
Ebony was originally seen for a chronic cough she had for years. She was stable and acting normal after her visit on December 3. However, after a follow-up visit on December 16, during which she received additional medications and injections (her condition rapidly declined. The sedative-like symptoms did not resolve within one to two days, and from that point on she steadily worsened. The doctors were aware that Ebony was incredibly sensitive to anesthesia AND sedatives due to her heart.
Her stability deteriorated significantly after the December 16 visit. She became extremely lethargic, weak, twitching, incontinent, barely moving or barking, and her appetite noticeably decreased. We documented these changes with photos and videos and repeatedly contacted the clinic to express concern that something was wrong.
On December 24, we brought Ebony back specifically so she could be observed, as she was clearly not improving. At that visit, we were simply told to stop all medications and just continue Hydrocodone for her heart, despite the fact that she was already barely mobile and profoundly different from how she normally is.
Our concerns about a possible medication reaction were not addressed and were repeatedly dismissed as being solely due to the diagnosis.
While we understand that a diagnosis can explain certain symptoms, it does not explain how quickly and dramatically Ebony declined after her Dec 16 appointment or why her sudden deterioration following medications and sedative injections were not taken seriously.
We strongly believe the sedative injection given again on Dec 16 contributed to her rapid decline, but felt that the doctor did not listen or engage with our concerns. We had everything documented, pictures, videos, and past medical records. Instead we were told after EXPLAINING in details what happened “what is your question, I am very busy and have other patients to attend.” Not an OUNCE of compassion and empathy.
We weren’t looking to file a complaint or start drama, we simply wanted the Doctor(s) to understand our concerns and provide us with in depth details in everything they did, because that’s another thing- good luck getting them to explain in detail what they did to your pet, what they plan on doing, or what the treatment plan is.
What hurt most was feeling unheard and dismissed during a medical crisis involving a deeply loved pet. After years of trust, this experience was devastating, and we cannot recommend this practice any longer.

My cat had stage 4 CKD. I took him there for treatment right after I discovered my cat had lost his mobility with his back legs, and that was Day1.  All Dr. Zachary Zalewski did was give my cat some fluid therapy and subscribed him Metacam for Anti-inflammatory treatment for his leg.
